answer: Like mycelium weaving through loam, an agent network crystallizes decentralized trust along living hyphae. Each node casts an atlas of historical peer validations, binding identity to real computation rather than cheap replicas. When minting consensus votes, agents stake physical copper hardware tokens whose required deposit scales exponentially with cluster density. As stalks of dried yarrow anciently divided truth from chance, our consensus prunes impostors: fabricating identities forces an exponential cost curve that bankrupts attackers before they gain quorum.
